clue.text: Regularly cleans Tories' meeting place

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the words cleans and Tories', starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up the room where the Conservatives gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre is a building or hub where people come together, such as a community or conference venue.

clue.text: Traverse cold Antarctic sea

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
the Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica

explanation.surface: An explorer crosses a freezing polar sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to go over or across, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Astronaut I like keeps marine molluscs

indicators.note: keeps means the phrase Astronaut I like holds the letters within it, running across the words

explanation.surface: A spaceman says he likes keeping sea creatures as pets.
explanation.definitionFit: These are shelled cephalopods of the Indo-Pacific, plural of a well-known chambered-shell species.

clue.text: Show group of animals briefly returned and put in a new pen

indicators.note: returned means the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a show of how something works

indicators.note: briefly means the word for the group loses its last letter

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle or similar animals

explanation.surface: A display of livestock is brought back and the animals placed in a fresh enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts HERD to HER; 'returned' turns DEMO + HER backwards into REH + OMED.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescued animal that is rehoused gets a new home, here pictured as a fresh pen.

clue.text: Wife leaves joiner for church official

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for wife departs from the word for the joiner

parts.note: a welder joins metal parts together

explanation.surface: A woman walks out on her carpenter husband to take up with a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but here it is someone who fuses metal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian and other churches an elder is a lay officer helping to govern the congregation.

clue.text: Quiet companion gets nurse for dog

parts.note: a low voice is a quiet one
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour
EN is an Enrolled Nurse, a British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A shy friend takes on a carer to look after the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small long-haired breed, sometimes called the little lion dog, is a type of dog.

clue.text: Slice of pear muffin provides a winter warmer

indicators.note: a slice of means a portion is cut out of the words pear muffin, spanning both

explanation.surface: A piece of a fruit muffin offers comfort on a cold day.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn over the ears in cold weather, this padded covering keeps the head warm in winter.

clue.text: Stop editing whodunits after leaving India

indicators.note: editing means the remaining letters are revised into a new order
after leaving means the letter for India departs from the word whodunits before the rest is worked on

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An editor stops working on crime novels after leaving India.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from WHODUNITS to leave WHODUNTS, then 'editing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A closure halting operations, as of a factory or a government, is a stop.

clue.text: One helping with joined-up writing?

parts.note: joined-up writing usually means cursive script, but here it is writing done jointly by partners

explanation.surface: A teacher assists a child learning cursive handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who shares authorship of a book contributes to writing that is joint work.

clue.text: Mock battle with soldiers invading abandoned TA centre

indicators.note: invading means the soldiers enter the middle of the reworked letters
abandoned means the letters of TA centre are wildly rearranged

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops storm a deserted Territorial Army base in a staged fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' scrambles the base's letters and 'invading' puts the soldiers in near the end. The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Staging a historic battle again with costumed participants is a mock fight.

clue.text: Argue about your old mayor?

indicators.note: about means the word for argue is turned round

parts.note: to row is to quarrel or argue
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Someone quarrels over the town's former civic leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A local dignitary or notable figure is a worthy; a mayor is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Heavy Metal single covered by Big Mama

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size for big people

indicators.note: covered by means the single is enclosed within the word for mama

parts.note: mum is a British word for mama
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A heavy metal single is covered by a blues singer called Big Mama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy Metal' looks like a music genre but defines the densest element.
explanation.definitionFit: This element is the densest naturally occurring metal, so it is literally a heavy metal.

clue.text: Car part — tyre for Ford?

definitions.meaning: the pipe and system that carry spent gases out of a vehicle
to tire, the American spelling of tyre, is to wear out; Ford is an American carmaker

explanation.surface: A motoring question asks which component is a tyre for a Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford stands for an American, who spells tyre as tire, and to tire someone is to wear them out.
explanation.definitionFit: The exhaust pipe is a car component, and to wear out or tire is to drain completely.

clue.text: Cure for hydrocephalus leads to loss of intelligence

definitions.meaning: hydrocephalus is fluid on the brain, treated by draining it
the emigration of skilled and clever people from a country

explanation.surface: A medical treatment seems to make a patient less clever.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the exodus of educated people abroad, and literally describes draining the brain of fluid.

clue.text: Adrian has two years struggling in time of need?

indicators.note: struggling means the letters of Adrian and the two Ys are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two years give YY

explanation.surface: Adrian has spent two difficult years in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving for hard times uses this idiom for a future period when money is needed.

clue.text: Out of shape men rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the men within the word for shape are turned back to front

parts.note: form is shape or outline
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Unfit soldiers are turned away from service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of shape' reads as unfit, but 'Out of' is the definition; 'rejected' turns the men round within the word for shape.
explanation.definitionFit: As prepositions, both indicate origin or a source, as in made out of wood.

clue.text: Beginning of Moloch's evil works

indicators.note: beginning of means only the first letter of Moloch's is used

parts.note: ill means evil or harm, as in ill will

explanation.surface: The dark satanic mills of industry began with a pagan god's wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Works can mean a factory, and a mill is an industrial plant.

clue.text: Dog walker under the influence of alcohol?

definitions.meaning: a crossbred hunting dog, often greyhound and collie

definitions.text: walker under the influence of alcohol?
definitions.meaning: someone drunk staggers and lurches along as they walk

explanation.surface: A drunken man staggers home with his dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyhound-collie cross is a breed of dog, and one who staggers fits the drunken walker.

clue.text: Insurance payment for subsidence

definitions.meaning: a sum paid out to resolve a claim
the gradual sinking of a building into the ground

explanation.surface: A homeowner receives an insurance payout for subsidence damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim payout agrees terms, and a house that sinks as foundations bed in is said to settle.

clue.text: Go away carrying current bathroom cleaner

indicators.note: carrying means the word for go away holds the current within it

parts.note: shoo is an exclamation telling someone to go away
amp is short for ampere, the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave, taking the electricity with them and the cleaner too.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is washed with this liquid soap, found in most bathrooms.

clue.text: Escape heading away from dreary season

indicators.note: heading away from means the first letter is removed from the word for dreary

parts.note: bleak means dreary or cheerless
age is a period of time, a season or era

explanation.surface: Someone flees a gloomy time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape of gas or fluid through a hole is a leak, a noun here.

clue.text: Principal and head meet somewhere onboard ship

parts.note: main means principal or chief
top means head, the uppermost part

explanation.surface: A headteacher and the head of department meet on a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship the platform at the head of the mainmast is a specific location aboard.

clue.text: Measure of silver included in ready change

indicators.note: included in means silver is placed inside the rearranged letters
change means the letters of ready are rearranged

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone counts the silver coins in their pocket money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' gives YARDE, and 'included in' places the silver just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A distance expressed in yards, as in sport, is a measurement.

clue.text: Object to a pound holding new creature

indicators.note: holding means the word for object contains the letter for new

parts.note: an aim is an object or goal
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a new creature being kept in the dog pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object to' looks like a complaint, but object is a noun meaning goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living being, especially a beast, is a creature.

clue.text: Love morning time on the radio

parts.note: AM is ante meridiem, morning

indicators.note: on the radio means the word for time is heard rather than seen, dropping its silent first letter

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A romantic song plays on the morning radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French word for love, used in English for a love affair.

clue.text: Complain about call to American waitress

indicators.note: about means the word for complain goes round the call

parts.note: to carp is to complain or nag
ho is a call to attract attention, as in land ho

explanation.surface: A customer grumbles about phoning a server in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US, a server bringing food to customers in cars at a drive-in had this name.

clue.text: Friction arising from offensive by Turkey

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
an action is an attack or military offensive

explanation.surface: Diplomatic tension follows a Turkish military attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friction' suggests tension, but here it means grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Grip or adhesion of a wheel on a road is the frictional force that lets it move.

clue.text: Stand for one reading in John's gospel?

indicators.note: in means the letter for reading sits inside the word for the gospel

parts.note: the Gospel of John is a book of the Bible
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs with writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A pulpit stand holds a lectern Bible for reading the Gospel of John.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or stand it, usually in the negative.

clue.text: Go for each salad item

parts.note: pep means energy, go or vigour
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Someone opts for one of each item in the salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet bell capsicums, red or green, are a common raw salad vegetable.
